Erase counts are lifetime totals per block (all phases). WA = NAND page programs (host + GC) / host page writes, measured over the measurement phase only. GC is foreground and runs once per host block opened in steady state (1000/64 = 15.6 episodes per 1k writes in every configuration), so GC frequency is reported as blocks erased per 1k host writes.

## Sanity check against the analytic FIFO model (single write frontier)

Model: u = exp(-alpha (1 - u)), WA = 1/(1 - u), alpha = physical/logical pages. Assumptions: uniform random overwrites, one write stream, FIFO cleaning. Only the single-frontier FIFO column matches all assumptions; greedy and the dual-frontier main runs are shown for context. In steady state this FTL always keeps one erased block in reserve (it holds no data and is outside the write cycle), so the corrected column uses alpha' = (blocks - 1) / logical blocks.

| spare | OP | alpha | FIFO model WA | model, 1 block excluded | FIFO single-frontier WA | vs model | vs model (1 block excluded) | greedy single-frontier WA | FIFO dual WA | greedy dual WA |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|

| 72 | 7.6% | 1.0756 | 7.286 | 7.379 | 7.378 | +1.3% | -0.0% | 6.676 | 7.433 | 6.716 |

## GC reserve rule at experiment geometry (spare 72, seeds 1-3)

Page-granular reserve (default) vs the original rule that required two whole free blocks before the host could open one. On a 12-block device the old rule made greedy relocate 384 instead of 256 pages per 400 writes (tools/gc_trace.c); at this geometry the difference is:

| workload | policy | WA page-granular | WA whole-block | difference |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| uniform | greedy | 6.7164 | 6.7207 | +0.06% |
| uniform | fifo | 7.4233 | 7.4253 | +0.03% |
| hotcold | greedy | 6.7952 | 6.8002 | +0.07% |
| hotcold | fifo | 7.6807 | 7.6811 | +0.01% |
